title: pollCompletions re-introduces an auto-requeue path that can DOUBLE-PAY when the UNVERIFIED queryStatus misclassifies a succeeded GMO bulk transfer (or one item of it) as 'failed'.
description: FIND-B's safety thesis was: after a bank submit the outcome is unknown, so NEVER auto-requeue. pollCompletions (bank-payout-watcher.mjs:95-105) deliberately re-opens an auto-requeue lever: queryStatus(row.ref)==='failed' -> requeue(row.id) -> status back to 'queued' -> the next pass() re-claims and RE-SUBMITS the recipient = a second irreversible bank transfer = DOUBLE-PAY. The entire safety of this lever rests on queryStatus correctly distinguishing GMO failure from success, and queryStatus is EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED (line 133: 'GMO bulktransfer/status — UNVERIFIED endpoint/shape until live token'). Two concrete double-pay mechanics: (1) BATCH-vs-ITEM granularity: queryStatus queries by apptransferNo (the batch ref) and collapses the whole batch to ONE status via j.status||j.transferStatus, then pollCompletions applies that single verdict to EVERY 'submitted' row whose notes carry that ref. GMO 一括振込 status is per-item; a batch that is partially or wholly settled but whose batch-level field matches /fail|error|reject|失敗|却下/ (e.g. a transient '組戻'/'返却'/'エラー' substring in an unrelated field, or a recall of ONE item) causes ALL recipients of that batch to be requeued and re-paid. (2) requeue() (line 147) does NOT clear the stale ';ref=R1' from notes, and on re-submit markPaid overwrites notes with a NEW ref; the idempotency defense is the only backstop and it is doubly weak: GMO honoring x-idempotency-key is UNVERIFIED (line 46/88), AND idempotencyKey is computed over the NEW batch's {to,amount} (bank-payout-watcher.mjs:47-50) which changes whenever the recipient set or per-amount changes (per-amount = floor(balance/n), so a changed balance yields a different key) -> different key -> not deduped -> double-pay. The unit test (bank-payout-watcher.test.js:41-54) only exercises a clean 1-ref-per-row 'failed' string and proves nothing about batch/item granularity or a misclassified-success requeue. Net: this is the single largest residual money-doubling path; it converts an UNVERIFIED external status read directly into an irreversible re-payment with no human gate.
recommendation: Do NOT auto-requeue on a 'failed' read from an unverified endpoint. Either (a) route a GMO-confirmed failure to 'needs_review' (operator confirms the funds did NOT leave, then manually re-queues), mirroring FIND-003's no-auto-pay policy; or (b) gate requeue behind a per-ITEM (not per-batch) confirmation AND clear the ref + write a fresh idempotency key that is stable across balance changes (key on funding wake + recipient id, not on amount). Add tests for: a batch ref shared by multiple submitted rows, a misclassified-success status string, and proof that a requeued row cannot be re-submitted with a colliding idempotency key.
